November 7, 2026

Trump orders Justice Department to pursue Democrats over impeachment threats

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

In a lengthy Truth Social post, President Trump said Democratic political leaders have been sending threatening letters to officials including the Attorney General, raising impeachment and other punishment. He called it a criminal act and said imprisonment should be on the table for what he described as extortionists, urging Republicans to act quickly. Trump said he was ordering the Department of Justice to look into the matter immediately, and offered no evidence for the claims. The post came days after Democrats swept the midterm elections.

Stephen Miller named chief of staff as House Republicans demand his removal

tags: politics, immigration
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump has installed Stephen Miller as chief of staff and, according to reporting in The Atlantic, wants him to "crack skulls" rather than be reined in, including potentially targeting journalists. Miller has been the architect of the administration's mass deportation program. House Republicans responded publicly, with Rep. Marlin Stutzman of Indiana calling it a "horrible decision" and others expressing "utter disbelief" and saying Miller should be fired rather than promoted. Several said Trump is ignoring warnings that voters rejected the immigration crackdown.

Judge appoints special master to investigate whether DOJ lied over D.C. golf course

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Federal Judge Ana Reyes has appointed a former federal prosecutor as special master to investigate whether Trump's Department of Justice made false statements to the court in litigation over a proposed golf course redevelopment at East Potomac Park in Washington, D.C. The administration had told the court it was not pursuing redevelopment of the site. The court concluded that account may have been untrue and ordered the outside inquiry.

Houston mayor signs order limiting city cooperation with ICE

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @groundnews

Houston Mayor John Whitmire announced Friday that municipal officials would restrict assistance to federal immigration agents, following an election that gave Democrats control in Texas. Whitmire said enforcement would target immigrants who "pose a danger, not those that are going about their family business, work and education," and that traffic violations and offenses involving neither violence nor jail time would not trigger referrals to immigration authorities. An executive directive will set out the policy's terms. Houston, the fourth-largest U.S. city, is among the first municipalities seeking to constrain ICE after Tuesday's vote.

Senate bill would fast-track data centers and pipelines on public lands

tags: climate, tech, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (S. 5653), co-written by Sen. Mike Lee, could receive a Senate vote as soon as Monday. It would speed approval of gas pipelines serving large data centers, weaken NEPA, the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act, and cut the window to challenge a project in court from six years to 150 days. Judges who find a project broke the law could not halt construction, only remand it to the agency, and permits issued under current agencies would be difficult for a future administration to undo — potentially including Project Beehive, a plan for small nuclear reactors, data centers and nuclear waste storage on public land near Price, Utah. Senators may receive final text less than 24 hours before voting, and Republicans cannot pass it without Democratic votes.

Oil profits and gas prices draw scrutiny since start of Iran war

tags: markets, climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

American oil companies have recorded more than $130 billion in profit since the Iran war began, while the average family has paid roughly $1,100 extra for gas and diesel, with pump prices still near $4. Refiners are clearing about $62 a barrel on turning crude into gasoline, roughly double pre-war margins. Congress's Joint Economic Committee found Trump's oil and gas holdings grew by as much as $35.8 million this year, with 94% of his 2026 oil stock purchases made after the war started and sales of up to $1 million in Exxon stock on the day he announced a ceasefire; the White House says outside managers run his portfolio. Eleven fossil fuel donors contributed about $65 million to his political operation, and the Center for American Progress estimates they received $31 billion in tax breaks and rollbacks.

CENTCOM offers $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear program

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

U.S. Central Command said the Rewards for Justice program is offering up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program. The offer covers facilities, equipment and associated personnel, including members of the scientific community, as well as the movement of any of those. Tips are being accepted through the Rewards for Justice website.

Democrat leads Mississippi Senate race after flipping Forrest County

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Scott Colom leads the Mississippi Senate race against Cindy Hyde-Smith, with his margin widening as counting continues. According to the Mississippi Free Press, Colom carried Forrest County — named for Ku Klux Klan founder Nathan Bedford Forrest — by about 10 points, a 29-point swing from Trump's 18-point win there. The race has not been called, and a final result is not expected until November 10.

Democrats win Arizona legislature and governorship for first time since 1966

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Arizona voters gave Democrats majorities in both state legislative chambers alongside another term for Gov. Katie Hobbs, putting all three under Democratic control for the first time since 1966. The Associated Press confirmed the legislative turnover through race calls Friday. Republicans lost a House majority held for six decades and a Senate majority dating to the 1990s.

Kansas elects Democrat Cindy Holscher as governor

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Cindy Holscher, the Democratic nominee for governor of Kansas, has won the race according to VoteHub. The state will continue to have a Democratic governor and also has a Democratic senator. The result adds to Democratic gains in the midterm elections.

Trump offers press secretary job to UFC chief Dana White

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

Trump announced on Truth Social that he had offered the White House press secretary role to UFC head Dana White, asking him to bring fighters including Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov and Amanda Nunes as assistants "to defend us against the Lunatic Left." The White House did not answer questions about the post and no official confirmed the offer; CNN later reported White had declined, though he was subsequently said to be flying to Washington to meet Trump on Monday. Observers noted that Dana W. White, a woman, previously served as Assistant to the Secretary of Defense for Public Affairs and Pentagon chief spokesperson, prompting speculation that Trump offered the job to the wrong person after seeing the name on a shortlist. Trump has had no permanent spokesperson since Karoline Leavitt left in August; her successor Katie Zacharia held the role for five days.

Trump reported furious with staff and planning further cabinet purges

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump has spent several days shouting at aides behind the scenes over Tuesday's election losses, according to the Daily Beast and other outlets, including at departing chief of staff Susie Wiles. He has said he will fire additional cabinet members. Reports describe a somber mood inside the White House, with Trump blaming those around him for the result.

Democrats signal criminal contempt and jail time for defied subpoenas

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Congressional Democrats are indicating they will pursue criminal contempt against Republicans who defy subpoenas. Rep. Yassamin Ansari said at an event that jail time should be on the table and that officials avoiding subpoenas now could face prosecution under a future administration. The statute of limitations for criminal contempt extends beyond two years.

Laura Loomer reported to have been paid for political posts, fueling dark money scrutiny

tags: media, politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

A Wall Street Journal exclusive reported that Trump ally Laura Loomer was paid thousands of dollars for political posts, information attributed to people familiar with the situation and confirmed by other outlets. The New Republic reported that a Trump administration adviser exposed the arrangement and that some of her most inflammatory posts were paid for; Loomer has announced a hiatus from social media. The reporting has intensified questions about undisclosed funding of political content creators through 501(c)(4) organizations, which are not required to reveal donors. Similar transparency questions have been directed at Chorus, a 501(c)(4) that pays creator stipends reported at $5,000 a month for 15 hours of work under an incubator program and $2,000 a month for five hours under an accelerator program, without requiring participants to disclose their involvement.

Pro-Israel groups claim broad success across midterm races

tags: politics, defence
sources: @ericmoutsos

AIPAC said at least 234 of its endorsed candidates won election nationwide in the 2026 midterms, while J Street endorsed more than 200 House and Senate candidates and reported 98% of them winning. Hakeem Jeffries, who has defended Israeli policy and backed continued U.S. military assistance while opposing efforts to cut that funding, is positioned to become Speaker of the House after Democrats won back the chamber. The claim advanced is that both parties' leadership share the same position on U.S. support for Israel.

Trump Media stock falls to record low after election

tags: markets, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

DJT stock has fallen to a record post-election low, with Reuters reporting investors have lost more than $2 billion. Trump holds a stake valued at about $460 million, and his net worth has declined along with the share price.

Polling cited against Jeffries and Schumer retaining Democratic leadership

tags: politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Figures circulated after the midterms put Trump's approval rating at 31%, Hakeem Jeffries' at 18% and Chuck Schumer's at 13%. The argument advanced is that elevating Jeffries and Schumer into leadership positions would disenfranchise the voters who delivered the midterm victory.

Utah clean energy program adds $4 charge to power bills in January

tags: climate, energy
sources: @carolinegleich

Rocky Mountain Power customers who received a recent letter about a new clean energy program are automatically enrolled, and a $4 monthly charge will appear on bills starting in January. The program funds new wind and solar generation in the region and took Utah communities about ten years to establish; the fee is expected to drop after two years. Customers who take no action remain enrolled, and households that apply for Utah's HEAT program are signed up for HELP and receive the clean energy program at no cost.
